titulo: AI Shockwaves and Midterm Upheavals Grip Global Markets
resumo: November 2026 delivered an extraordinary combination of political shifts, corporate crises, and shifting monetary expectations that tested investor resolve. The **US midterm elections** delivered a decisive Democratic sweep of Congress, sparking an initial relief rally before triggering profound anxiety over potential AI regulations and data-center crackdowns. This regulatory unease quickly deepened into a historic tech rout as corporate governance scandals at **Nvidia** culminated in the departure of CEO Jensen Huang. Meanwhile, persistent inflation pressures pushed government bond yields higher, prompting markets to price in more aggressive central bank action. Despite this heavy volatility, broader market indices demonstrated surprising resilience, underpinned by robust corporate updates and significant primary market activity.

sumup.frase: Markets navigated intense volatility driven by **AI regulatory fears** and executive shakeups.
sumup.porque: Investors weighed political shifts and tech governance shocks against persistent inflation and rising bond yields.

drivers.texto: Democrats flipped control of Congress in the midterms, initially sparking a broad relief rally before fueling concerns over stricter data-center moratoriums and AI regulation. The S&P 500 rose +0.2% this month to reach 7592.4 by November 12, though the Nasdaq Composite slipped -0.3% to 25366.09 amid tech sector turbulence.

Nvidia shares plunged as an internal investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a Chinese executive led to his resignation, with CFO Colette Kress stepping in as interim chief. This governance shock rattled artificial intelligence sentiment, contributing to a -3.7% decline in the VIX equity volatility index to 18.7 as traders hedged against further tech sell-offs.

drivers.factor: Hot Inflation and Rate Hike Fears
drivers.texto: Hotter-than-expected inflation data revived market expectations of tighter monetary policy, driving US Treasury yields sharply higher. The US 2-year Treasury yield climbed +30bp this month to 4.86, while the 10-year yield rose +16bp to 5.1.

drivers.factor: Crude Oil Plummets on Mideast Hopes
drivers.texto: Brent crude oil tumbled -23.3% this month to 92.14 dollars a barrel as diplomatic progress and hopes of de-escalation in Iran eased Middle East supply disruption fears. This sharp slide helped alleviate broader cost pressures across global supply chains.

Euro area AAA 2-year yields rose +7bp this month to 3.0751, while 10-year yields remained steady at 3.3672. Meanwhile, the EUR/USD exchange rate fell -1.1% this month to 1.1052 as the US dollar reacted to shifting domestic political dynamics.

themes.texto: The artificial intelligence boom faced a multi-front reckoning this month, combining political pushback from newly empowered Democrats with unprecedented corporate turmoil. While mega-deals like Marvell's acquisition and Anthropic's blockbuster IPO filing showcased enduring demand, soaring compute costs and data-center opposition exposed credit vulnerabilities. High-yield credit spreads tightened -24bp to 3.2, yet investors increasingly scrutinized the heavy debt loads supporting the AI buildout.

Inflation persistence continued to challenge central banks, with euro area inflation standing at 4% and Portuguese inflation at 3.9% in October 2026. Higher price prints reignited rate-hike debates globally, reflected in the ECB deposit rate holding at 2.5% and the 12-month Euribor averaging 3.239%. Bond investors demanded higher compensation for sovereign debt, driving US and European borrowing costs upward.

Corporations actively restructured operations to cope with rising funding costs and shifting regulatory landscapes, marked by major breakups such as CVS Health splitting its pharmacy and insurance businesses. Private equity and M&A pipelines remained active despite tightening credit conditions, though tech firms faced heightened scrutiny over supply chain compliance and export controls to China.

questoes.q: Can the artificial intelligence market sustain its massive infrastructure spending without Jensen Huang at Nvidia?
questoes.porque: Jensen Huang was widely viewed as the central pillar and visionary promoter of the global AI hardware boom.
questoes.sinais: Upcoming earnings reports and guidance from major cloud hyperscalers regarding their AI capital expenditure budgets.

questoes.q: Will the Democratic sweep in the US midterms result in crippling federal curbs on data centers?
questoes.porque: Elected officials face intense local pressure over power consumption, grid reliability, and environmental impacts of AI facilities.
questoes.sinais: Introduction and progression of specific federal regulatory bills targeting data-center expansion and energy consumption.

questoes.q: Are central banks finished raising interest rates in the face of sticky inflation prints?
questoes.porque: Hotter consumer price data has revived market fears of a renewed tightening cycle by the Federal Reserve and peers.
questoes.sinais: Upcoming employment, wage tracker, and monthly consumer price index releases.

momentos.facto: Marvell agreed to acquire Lumentum in a landmark technology deal, while oil tumbled on US-Iran peace hopes.
US stock markets surged in a broad relief rally after Democrats swept control of Congress in the midterm elections.
The Nasdaq suffered its biggest daily drop in 19 months as tech stocks lost 2.3 trillion dollars amid AI regulatory fears.
Hotter-than-expected US inflation data sparked sharp spikes in Treasury bond yields and renewed rate-hike concerns.
Nvidia shares plunged as CEO Jensen Huang resigned amid an internal investigation into his relationship with a corporate executive.
